(d) At ωr, impedance of the circuit is 0.

questions.solution:
The impedance of an AC circuit is given by, Z=R2+XC-XL2.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Maximum power is dissipated in a circuit containing an inductor, a capacitor and a resistor connected in series with an AC source, when resonance occurs.

Statement II: Maximum power is dissipated in a circuit containing pure resistor due to zero phase difference between current and voltage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
questions.solution:
The formula for impedance is given by 

Z=R2+XL-XC2

At resonance, XL=XC. So, Zmin=R

Power will be maximum when impedance is minimum. Thus the maximum power occurs in a purely resistive circuit.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I : When the frequency of an AC source in a series LCR circuit increases, the current in the circuit first increases, attains a maximum value and then decreases.

Statement II : In a series LCR circuit, the value of power factor at resonance is one.

In the light of given statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
When an a.c. voltage is applied in a series LCR circuit, the current is increased first, attains a maximum and then decreases.

The formula to calculate the power factor is given by

cosϕ=RR2+XL2-XC2   ...1

At resonance, XL=XC, Hence,

cosϕresonance=1

Thus, both the statements are true.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I: The reactance of an ac circuit is zero. It is possible that the circuit contains a capacitor and an inductor.
Statement-II: In ac circuit, the average power delivered by the source never becomes zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.solution:
The reactance of a circuit containing a capacitor and an inductor is given by X=XL-XC=ωL-1ωC. An AC circuit has zero reactance at resonance, i.e., when, XL=XC. So, first statement is true.

The power consumption in an AC circuit is zero when circuit contains only inductance or capacitance since average power consumed in a cycle is zero for inductance or capacitance. So, second statement is false.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In an LCR series circuit, current is maximum at resonance.
Statement II: Current in a purely resistive circuit can never be less than that in a series LCR circuit when connected to same voltage source.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution:
Statement-I $I_m=\frac{V_m}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(X_L-X_C\right)^2}}$ at resonance $X_L=X_C$ Thus, $I_m=\frac{V_m}{R}\because$ Impendence is minimum therefore $I$ is maximum at resonance.
Statement-II $\mathrm{I}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)$ in purely resistive circuit.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : An AC circuit undergoes electrical resonance if it contains either a capacitor or an inductor.

Statement II: An AC circuit containing a pure capacitor or a pure inductor consumes high power due to its non-zero power factor. In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but statement II is true
Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
For resonance to occur the condition is XL=XC.

So, both inductor and capacitor is required.

The power factor is given by cosϕ.

For an inductor the power factor is zero-lagging, cos90°=0. The angle between the voltage and current is 90°.

For a capacitor the power factor is zero-leading.

Hence, both statements are false.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Smaller the band width, sharper the resonance and easier it is to tune an LCR circuit.
Reason (R) : Resonant frequency is arithmetic mean of half power frequencies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) states that a smaller bandwidth leads to sharper resonance and easier tuning of an LCR circuit, which is true. A smaller bandwidth means a sharper peak in the resonance curve.
Reason (R) claims that the resonant frequency is the arithmetic mean of half-power frequencies, which is also true. However, this does not directly explain why a smaller bandwidth results in sharper resonance.
Thus, while both statements are true, the reason does not effectively explain the assertion. Therefore, the correct choice is:
(2) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

Reason (R) : The impedance of series LCR circuit depends over angular frequency of applied emf.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true because the impedance of a series L-C-R circuit can vary depending on the relationship between inductive reactance, capacitive reactance, and resistance. Reason (R) is also true, as the impedance does depend on the angular frequency. However, (R) does not explain (A) because it doesn't clarify why impedance can be greater, equal, or less than resistance; it only states that impedance varies with frequency.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : In a series LCR circuit at resonance, the voltage across the capacitor or inductor may be more than the applied voltage.
Reason (R) : At resonance in a series LCR circuit, the voltages across inductor and capacitor are equal & \(180^{\circ}\) out of phase.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true because at resonance, the voltage across the capacitor or inductor can exceed the applied voltage. Reason (R) is also true, as the voltages across the inductor and capacitor are equal in magnitude and \(180^{\circ}\) out of phase at resonance. However, (R) does not explain why the voltages can be greater than the applied voltage; it simply describes their relationship.

Assertion (A) : In an LC oscillation energy is not constant practically.
Reason (R) : Energy is lost in resistance of inductor and of connecting wires and also in form of electromagnetic radiations.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true because, in practical LC oscillations, energy is not constant due to losses. Reason (R) is also true as energy is lost in the resistance of the inductor, connecting wires, and as electromagnetic radiation, which explains why the energy is not constant.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Average power consumed in an ac circuit is equal to average power consumed by resistors in the circuit.
Reason (R) : Average power consumed by capacitor and inductor is zero
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A): Average power consumed in an AC circuit is equal to average power consumed by resistors in the circuit.
- This statement is true. In an AC circuit, only the resistive components consume average power. Capacitors and inductors do not consume power; they only store and release energy.
Reason (R): Average power consumed by the capacitor and inductor is zero.
- This statement is also true. Capacitors and inductors exchange energy with the circuit but do not dissipate power as heat; therefore, their average power consumption over a complete cycle is zero.
Now, assessing the relationship between the two statements:
- Both statements are true, and (R) correctly explains (A) because the zero average power of capacitors and inductors means that the average power in the circuit is indeed equal to that consumed by resistors.
Thus, the correct choice is:
(1) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Resonance occurs in a series LCR circuit when the frequency of the applied emf is 1000 Hz. Then

& V_1=\sqrt{V_R^2+V_L^2}=100 \quad \ldots (1) \\
& V_C-V_L=120 \quad \ldots (2) \\

& V_L=50 \sqrt{3} V=86.6 \mathrm{~V} ~\&~ V_C=206.6 \mathrm{~V} \\
& \cos \phi=\frac{V_R}{130}=\frac{5}{13}
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q:
A series LCR circuit is connected to a 45 sin(ωt) Volt source. The resonant angular frequency of the circuit is 105 rad s−1 and current amplitude at resonance is I0. When the angular frequency of the source is ω=8×104 rad s−1, the current amplitude in the circuit is 0.05 I0. If L=50 mH, match each entry in List-I with an appropriate value from List-II and choose the correct option.

  List-I   List-II
P I0 in mA 1 44.4
Q The quality factor of the circuit 2 18
R The bandwidth of the circuit in rad s−1 3 400
S The peak power dissipated at resonance in Watt 4 2250
    5 500
questions.solution:
Resonant angular frequency is given by, 1LC=105

150×10-3C=105⇒C=2×10-9 F

Given: V=45sinωt. Therefore, V0=45.

Now, I0=V0R=45R               ...ii

Inductive reactance, XL=ωL=8×104×50×10-3=4000 Ω.

and capacitive reactance, XC=1ωC=18×104×2×10-9=6250 Ω.

For new current amplitude, we can write

0.05I0=45R2+XL-XC2⇒0.05I0=45R2+6250-40002⇒0.05×45R=45R2+6250-40002⇒R2+6250-40002=R20.052⇒R2+22502=400R2⇒R=2250399=112.67 Ω

Where XL0=XC0 are at resonant frequencies

On solving, ⇒I0=45R≃400 mA

Quality factor Q=XLR≃44.44

Now, Q=ω0∆ω⇒∆ω≃2250 rad s-1.

Peak power =45×4001000 W=18 W

Therefore, P→3, Q→1, R→4, S→2.

questions.q:
When an inductor of inductance \(\frac{6}{\pi} \mathrm{H}\), a capacitor of capacitance \(\frac{50}{\pi} \mu \mathrm{F}\) and resistor of resistance \(R\) are connected in series with an AC supply of rms voltage \(220 \mathrm{~V}\) and frequency \(50 \mathrm{~Hz}\), the rms current through the circuit is \(440 \mathrm{~mA}\). Match the inductive reactance, \(X_L\) the capacitive reactance, \(X_C\) the resistance \(R\) and the impedance \(Z\) of the circuit given in List-I with the corresponding values given in List-II.
\(\begin{array}{llll} \hline & \text { List- I } & & \text { List- II } \\ \hline \text {(A) } & X_L & \text { (i) } & 200 \Omega \\ \hline \text {(B) } & X_C & \text { (ii) } & 300 \Omega \\ \hline \text {(C) } & R & \text { (iii) } & 500 \Omega \\ \hline \text {(D) } & Z & \text { (iv) } & 600 \Omega \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Given, inductance of inductor, \(L=\frac{6}{\pi} \mathrm{H}\), 
capacitance of capacitor, \(C=\frac{50}{\pi} \mu \mathrm{F}\) 
supply voltage, \(V_{\text {rms }}=220 \mathrm{~V}\), 
supply frequency, \(f=50 \mathrm{~Hz}\) 
and supply current, \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}=440 \mathrm{~mA}\) 
Now, (A) inductive reactance, \(X_L=\omega L\)
\(\begin{aligned}
X_L & =2 \pi f \times L \quad(\because \omega=2 \pi f) \\
& =2 \pi \times 50 \times \frac{6}{\pi}=600 \Omega \\
X_L & =600 \Omega
\end{aligned}\)
(B) Capacitance reactance, \(X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}=\frac{1}{2 \pi f C}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
X_C & =\frac{\pi \times 10^6}{2 \pi \times 50 \times 50} \\
\Rightarrow \quad X_C & =\frac{10^6}{2500 \times 2} \Rightarrow X_C=200 \Omega
\end{aligned}\)
(C) Resistance, \(R\)
\(\therefore\) Impedance of LCR circuit, \(Z^2=R^2+\left(X_L-X_C\right)^2\)
Putting the given values, we get
\(\begin{aligned}
(500)^2 & =R^2+(600-200)^2 \\
250000 & =R^2+(400)^2 \\
R^2 & =250000-160000 \\
R^2 & =90000 \Rightarrow R=300 \Omega
\end{aligned}\)
(D) Impedance,
\(Z=\frac{V_{\text {rms }}}{I_{\text {rms }}}=\frac{220}{440} \times 10^3 \Rightarrow Z=500 \Omega\)

& & & \text{sensitivity} \\
\hline
(C) & \text{More resistance} & (R) & \text{Have resonant frequency } \\
& & & \omega=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{LC}}} \\
& & & \text{with maximum current} \\

& \text{curve (I - f)}& & \\

questions.solution:
Column-I:
- (A) LCR circuits: These circuits have a resonant frequency (related to option R) and can indicate sensitivity (related to option Q).
(B) Inductor: An inductor is analogous to mass in physics, as it stores energy in a magnetic field (related to option S).
(C) More resistance: More resistance will flatten the resonant curve (related to option P) and indicates sensitivity (related to option Q).
(D) Radio Tuner's characteristic curve: This characteristic curve indicates the sharpness (related to option Q) and shows how current varies with frequency (related to option R).
Now, let's match them:
1. (A) LCR circuits - (R): Have resonant frequency with maximum current.
2. (B) Inductor - (S): Analogous to mass.
3. (C) More resistance - (P): Will be flattened.
4. (D) Radio Tuner's characteristic curve - (Q): Sharpness indicates sensitivity.
So the correct matching is:
(1) A-R, B-S, C-P, D-Q

Now, let's match them:
1. (a) In L-R series AC circuit - (q):
Current lags voltage by an angle less than \(\pi / 2\).
2. (b) In R-C series AC circuit - (r):
Current leads voltage by an angle less than \(\pi / 2\).
3. (c) In L-C series AC circuit (XL > XC)
- (p): Current lags voltage by \(\pi / 2\).
4. (d) In purely resistive AC circuit -
(s): Current and voltage are in phase.
So the correct matching is:
(1) a-q, b-r, c-p, d-s

questions.q:
Match the following
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
 & \text{Currents} & & \text{r.m.s. values} \\
\hline
(1) & x_{0}\sin \omega t & (i) & x_{0} \\
\hline
(2) & x_{0}\sin \omega t \cos \omega t & (ii) & \tfrac{x_{0}}{\sqrt{2}} \\
\hline
(3) & x_{0}\sin \omega t + x_{0}\cos \omega t & (iii) & \tfrac{x_{0}}{2\sqrt{2}} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
1. \(x_0 \sin (\omega t)\) :
This is a pure sinusoidal function.
The r.m.s. value of a sinusoidal function \(A \sin (\omega t)\) is \(A / \sqrt{2}\). So, the r.m.s. value of \(x_0 \sin (\omega t)\) is \(x_0 / \sqrt{2}\).
2. \(x_0 \sin (\omega t) \cos (\omega t)\) :
Using the trigonometric identity \(\sin (2 \omega t)=2 \sin (\omega t) \cos (\omega t)\), this can be rewritten as \(\frac{x_0}{2} \sin (2 \omega t)\), which is again a sinusoidal function. The r.m.s. value will be \(\frac{x_0}{2 \sqrt{2}}\).
3. \(x_0 \sin (\omega t)+x_0 \cos (\omega t)\) : This is a sum of two sinusoidal functions. The r.m.s. value of such a sum can befound by using 2 r.m.s. \(=\sqrt{\left(\frac{x_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\left(\frac{x_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}=\).
Now, match the r.m.s. values:
1. \(x_0 \sin (\omega t) \rightarrow x_0 / \sqrt{2} \rightarrow\) (ii)
2. \(x_0 \sin (\omega t) \cos (\omega t) \rightarrow x_0 / 2 \sqrt{2} \rightarrow\) (iii)
3. \(x_0 \sin (\omega t)+x_0 \cos (\omega t) \rightarrow x_0 \rightarrow\) (i)
The correct matching is:
(c) 1 . (ii), 2. (iii), 3. (i)
